title: Nearly 80 Years After Roswell, Japanese Monk Displays Object He Says Came From UFO Crash
excerpt: A fragment displayed in Japan is claimed to come from the 1947 Roswell incident, but its origin remains unverified without independent testing and reliable recovery records.
content:
A Japanese Buddhist monk has displayed a small object he claims came from the alleged 1947 Roswell UFO crash in New Mexico.

Nearly 80 years after the incident, however, no publicly available independent scientific analysis has established a connection between the fragment and the original debris.

Takano Josen, a Japanese science journalist and UFO researcher, presented the object during an episode of American Alchemy with Jesse Michels released on 24 November 2026. The fragment is reportedly kept at Cosmo Isle Hakui, a space science museum in Japan's Ishikawa Prefecture.

Takano said the material was collected during a Japanese expedition to a location in New Mexico that he believes was the actual crash site. His account challenges the official explanation of the Roswell incident, but the object's origins remain unverified.

How the Alleged Roswell UFO Fragment Reached Japan

Takano helped establish Cosmo Isle Hakui, which opened in 1996. Before developing the museum, he worked in television production and served temporarily as a local government employee in his hometown of Hakui.

During the interview, Takano recalled visiting a location in New Mexico with Jesse Marcel Jr., whose father was involved in the military's original recovery of the Roswell debris.

Takano maintains that the location differs from the site commonly identified with the incident.

He said a group involving Takeharu Mikami, editor of the Japanese magazine Mu, later visited the area and collected the fragment. The material was subsequently donated to the museum, according to the account presented during the interview.

Photographs shared during the episode reportedly show Mikami holding a piece of material in New Mexico.

They do not establish when the object arrived at the location or whether it was connected to the events of 1947.

What Happened at Roswell in 1947?

In July 1947, the US military recovered unusual debris from a ranch in New Mexico. Military authorities initially announced the recovery of a 'flying disc' before identifying the material as balloon equipment.

The contrasting announcements fuelled speculation that the US government had recovered an extraterrestrial spacecraft. Decades later, the US Air Force investigated the incident and published its findings in 1994.

The investigation concluded that the debris came from Project Mogul, a classified balloon-based research programme designed to detect Soviet nuclear tests. A separate government records investigation published in July 1995 examined the available documentation relating to the incident.

Has the Alleged UFO Fragment Been Scientifically Tested?

No publicly available independent laboratory report has established the origin of the fragment displayed in Japan. Michels also raised the need for scientific testing during the podcast episode.

Researchers could examine the object's chemical composition and physical structure to determine whether its characteristics match known materials.

Isotope analysis might also provide information about its origin, although unusual results alone would not establish an extraterrestrial connection.

Scientists would also need a documented history of the fragment's recovery, storage and transfer to Japan. Without such records, even identifying the material would not necessarily connect it to the Roswell incident.

July 2027 will mark the 80th anniversary of the military's recovery of debris in New Mexico. Until independent testing and reliable documentation become available, Takano's fragment remains an object of uncertain origin rather than authenticated evidence of a UFO crash.
